answers.why: The Assyrian invasion passes through Judah and fills the breadth of its land.
Isaiah and his children are signs among the people of Israel.
The word falls upon Israel, identified next as the people of Ephraim and Samaria.
Ephraim is explicitly included among all the people alongside Samaria's inhabitants.
Syrians and Philistines devour Israel, whose people then fail to return to the LORD.
Israel's head and tail are explained as its elders and false prophets.
Manasseh attacks Ephraim in communal strife, and both oppose Judah.
Ephraim is the community attacked by Manasseh in the described strife.
Ephraim attacks Manasseh, and the two communities unite against Judah.
Manasseh is the community attacked by Ephraim before both oppose Judah.
Judah is the kingdom opposed jointly by Manasseh and Ephraim.
The light of Israel parallels its Holy One, referring to the nation's God.
The surviving national remnant relies upon the LORD, the Holy One of Israel.
Israel is addressed as a multitude like the sea's sand from which a remnant returns.
